issues: CITATION: McCracken et al. arXiv:2505.18266 is confirmed; I fetched the abs and html pages this session. Title 'Uncovering a Universal Abstract Algorithm for Modular Addition in Neural Networks'. Authors McCracken, Moisescu-Pareja, Letourneau, Precup, Love. v1 dated 23 May 2025. The quotes on the floor(n/2)-to-fewer transition, 'we don't know why it occurs' and Cor 4.8 are all verbatim. The paper gives no threshold in a norm exponent. The existing refs.bib entry mccracken2025 has the wrong title and author ('Emergence of sparse and dense circuits...', 'McCracken, Andrew') and must be replaced. NUMERICS: the analytic bound is derived correctly from the proof-internal share floor. It uses ceil(8 ln p), while the theorem statement has 9 ln p; this mismatch is cosmetic. NEW: the O(1/log p) envelope is very loose. The exact thresholds give (s-1)*p = 3.83, 3.80, 3.71, 3.68, 3.68, 3.67, which is nearly constant, while (s-1)*ln p falls from 1.07 to 0.50. I computed a constructive upper bound on the dense threshold: the first s at which a vertex adjacent to the uniform vertex has smaller sum v^{1/s}. It gives (s-1)*p between 3.4 and 4.0 for every prime up to 113, e.g. s <= 1.0302 at p=113, where the analytic bound only gives s-1 <= 3.58. So the dense window empirically scales like about 3.5/p, not 1/log p. The paper should present O(1/log p) as a loose proven envelope, and may add the ~3.7/p empirical scaling and the one-pivot certificate. Script: items/r27-dense-window/adj_vertex_thresh.py. NOVELTY: no prior art found for a p-dependent window of full-support optimality. The math reformulation is: the cheapest weighted Cayley graph on Z_p with spectral gap >= 1 under a concave cost. I could NOT search it: the WebSearch session budget was exhausted (200/200) and the arXiv API returned 429. The verdict is therefore upheld at low confidence.
